Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Thompson, CFO; and Lisa Patel, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeFlow platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on four key areas: evolving our customer mix toward enterprise dominance, expanding our operating margins, strengthening our LTV to CAC ratio, and driving robust net revenue retention.

On customer mix, we're seeing accelerated enterprise adoption, bolstering our high-quality revenue base. Operating margins hit new highs through disciplined execution and leverage. Our LTV/CAC continues to improve, reflecting efficient growth dynamics. And NRR remains a standout, powered by expansions and low churn.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $115 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 84%, and operating income was $21 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

Before I dive into forward guidance, let me expand on those four key areas Sarah highlighted, starting with our customer mix trends between enterprise and SMB segments. As many of you know, CloudForge leads in AI-driven workflow orchestration for collaborative teams, powering over 12,500 customers worldwide with our flagship ForgeFlow platform. Customer mix serves as a vital leading indicator for sustainable SaaS growth, impacting metrics like ARR, net retention, and ACV expansion.

For Q3, the headline figures show enterprise customers—those with ACV above $100,000, often Fortune 1000 equivalents—now accounting for 68% of our total ARR of $420 million, or $285 million, up from 62% in Q3 FY2023 and 65% last quarter. That's 35% year-over-year growth in enterprise ARR alone. Meanwhile, our SMB segment—ACV under $100,000—makes up 32% at $135 million, with 15% YoY growth. Customer-wise, we added 45 net new enterprise logos, totaling 520, a 22% YoY rise, while SMB customers reached 12,000, up 12% YoY via self-serve channels.

This enterprise tilt stems from our 'Enterprise First' strategy since FY2022. Over the last 12 months, enterprise ARR grew 2.4 times faster than SMB, thanks to bigger deals and stronger expansion. Enterprise average ACV reached $275,000, up 18% YoY, with 75% of new bookings as multi-year contracts featuring inflation escalators—typically 3-5 years. SMB ACV holds at $14,000, but multi-year commitments climbed to 25% from under 10% two years back.

Enterprise is our NRR powerhouse, hitting 122% this quarter—every dollar from last year now generates $1.22 via upsells, cross-sells, and renewals. Highlights include ForgeAI, automating 40% of workflows for clients like a Big Four consultancy in a $2.8 million ACV deal. SMB NRR is solid at 108%, volume-based with gradual land-and-expand. Churn aligns too: enterprise logo churn under 3% annualized, SMB at 8%, matching benchmarks from ServiceNow and Workday.

We've bolstered enterprise features, like the GA of ForgeFlow Enterprise Shield—zero-trust security with FedRAMP Moderate and integrations to SAP SuccessFactors and Oracle HCM. This clinched 12 deals over $1 million ACV in financial services, echoing Atlassian's Jira Align success. For SMBs, our updated self-serve portal with AI chat boosted free-to-paid conversions by 28%. That said, we're prioritizing 'rising mid-market' at $50-100k ACV for optimal velocity and retention, dialing back pure SMB volume.

Regionally, North America (55% of ARR) saw enterprise mix at 75%, up from 68% YoY, fueled by AWS Marketplace co-sells with Snowflake. Despite layoff noise, CISOs prioritize AI orchestration for cost cuts—our RFP win rate vs. Pegasystems rose to 65%. EMEA (25% ARR) balances at 55/45 enterprise/SMB, SMB up 20% YoY in DACH via GDPR self-serve, with enterprise picking up post-Paris data center, like a FTSE 100 retailer. APAC (20% ARR, 45% YoY growth) is 60% enterprise-led, strong in Japan/Australia sovereign cloud, though SMB grew just 8% amid yen weakness.

This mix sets us for 25-28% ARR growth in FY2025, enterprise as flywheel. We're directing 60% of GTM to field sales and SEs in healthcare/manufacturing, where ForgeFlow's no-code AI yields 3-5x ROI on labor—IDC shows 35% faster processes vs. Appian. SMB risks exist in recession, but 115% overall NRR cushions. Goal: 75% enterprise by FY2026, Snowflake-style.

Turning to operating margin, our non-GAAP figure reached 18.2% for the quarter, a 420 basis point YoY expansion from 14.0% last year, and 110 basis points better sequentially from 17.1% prior. This is our eighth straight quarter of expansion, highlighting SaaS leverage as we scale CloudForge's AI collaboration platform.

Context: revenue at $115 million, up 28% YoY, with ARR growth of 26% to levels supporting our trajectory. Rule of 40 score at 62, topping peers amid S&M pressures at Salesforce/Workday.

Drivers: Gross margin GAAP 82%, non-GAAP 84%, up 200 bps YoY, cost of revenue down to 16% from 18%. Cloud costs optimized—70% on AWS Graviton/Google TPUs, cutting per-user hosting 15%. NRR of 118% from Enterprise AI Suite upsells grew gross profit 32% YoY sans cost spikes.

Sales & marketing leveraged to 32% of revenue, expenses up 18% YoY to $37 million, 300 bps better. PLG boosted freemium-to-paid to 22%, CAC down 12% to under $8,000/enterprise seat, payback 11 months vs. HubSpot's 14. Channels like Microsoft Teams/AWS contributed 15% new ARR. U.S. (65% revenue) over 40% S&M margins; EMEA (20%, +45% YoY) some investment offset; APAC (15%) 28% efficient.

R&D at 20% of revenue, $23 million up 22% YoY but flat seq., focused on GenAI co-pilot (beta to 40% customers, automating 25% workflows like ServiceNow Vancouver). Flat 1,200 engineers via GitHub Copilot, 35% more features/sprint.

G&A 8% or $9 million, 100 bps better, via automation and SBC normalization—no M&A dilution.

This shows profitability shift amid budget delays like ZoomInfo noted. $45 million annualized savings from 'Efficiency Reset'—10% headcount cut, vendor consolidation. Fixed costs dilute over 30% ARR CAGR.

Ahead: Q4 margin 19-20%, FY end 24%+, with $2.1B RPO (+32% YoY, 85% conversion), NRR via bundling, selective India hiring for sub-10% G&A. Enables $180M FCF (15% margin), $500M repurchases/M&A.

Next, our LTV/CAC ratio, a flywheel cornerstone. Healthy ratios above 3x signal efficiency, like Snowflake/HubSpot.

Q3 blended at 4.2x, up from 3.8x Q2, 20% YoY from 3.5x—sixth straight seq gain, top quartile per Bessemer Cloud Index.

LTV $148,000, cohort lifespan 52 months (from 46), via 118% NRR. Expansions in DevOps to AutoScale AI/ForgeGuard; 5-7% pricing hikes sans churn, Datadog-style.

CAC $35,200, down 8% QoQ, payback 11 months vs. 16 median. PLG: 62% new ARR self-serve, from 48% YoY.

Segments: Enterprise 5.1x ($285k LTV/$56k CAC), 28% ARR, CAC -15% YoY via ABM/AWS Snowflake. Mid/SMB 3.9x ($92k/$23.5k), PLG 14% conversions via ForgeAI Copilot (72% activation). AI/ML verticals 4.8x early.

Regions: NA 4.5x (68% ARR, 122% NRR, FedRAMP/SOC2). EMEA 3.9x from 3.2x (Dublin DC -35% latency). APAC 3.4x +25% YoY (Singapore/Tencent vs. Alibaba).

Bets: AI retention (92% churn predict, +18% tenure); channels 35% ACV, -40% CAC; cohorts 2024 at 4.6x. Rule 40 at 68 (45% growth +23% FCF).

Q4 guide 4.3-4.5x, $250M+ FCF for M&A like New Relic observability.

Finally, NRR at 118% dollar-based, up from 115% Q2, 112% YoY—top quartile Bessemer. Top 1,000 customers 128%, mid-market 110%; YTD $45M expansions, 28% of $320M Q3 ARR.

Expansion +28 pts (from +25): AnomalyForge AI 65% adoption, $75k upsells, $12M usage ARR (AWS Bedrock/Azure); cross-sell 72% enterprise (Stripe/Plaid SecurityForge SOC2/GDPR); seats +15% QoQ Slack/Teams.

Contraction -5 pts (from -6), usage in 2% variable ARR, fixed 85% buffer. QBRs saved 40% at-risk.

Churn -5 pts gross logo (1.2% monthly), 4% dollar; enterprise <0.5% annual (60% 3-yr auto-renew); mid 8% pricing sensitivity like HubSpot. U.S. 122%, EMEA 116% FS expansions, APAC 108% offset India 30% Reliance Jio.

CS headcount 250, AI health scores 95% renewals, 90-day predict. Q4 117-120%, upside GenAI/Federal CMMC. Platform flywheel vs. macro like ServiceNow.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $440 million to $450 million.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to register for questions, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, John. ForgeAI has been transformative, automating up to 40% of workflow decisions and driving key expansions. It's central to our 118% NRR, with 65% adoption among eligible customers contributing $12 million in incremental ARR from usage spikes. In enterprise deals, like our $2.8 million Big Four win, it fueled upsells averaging $75,000, while PLG conversions jumped 28% in SMB. Overall, it's accelerated ARR growth to 26% YoY, strengthened our 4.2x LTV/CAC, and positioned us for 25-28% growth next year by deepening multi-product adoption across DevOps, security, and collab tools.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion?

Lisa Patel:
Great question, Emily. International is a growth engine, now 45% of ARR with APAC up 45% YoY to 20% share. We're enterprise-heavy at 60% mix there, leveraging sovereign cloud in Japan/Australia. EMEA at 25% ARR holds 55/45 mix, SMB 20% YoY in DACH GDPR self-serve, enterprise accelerating post-Paris DC with FTSE wins. Key plans: Singapore localization, Tencent partnerships to counter Alibaba; Dublin DC cut latency 35% for Germany/UK; India via Reliance Jio for 30% growth. GTM 60% to verticals, hyperscaler co-sells like AWS Snowflake. Expect continued acceleration, targeting 117-120% NRR regionally.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment?

Mike Thompson:
Thanks, David. Churn remains best-in-class at 4% dollar-weighted, -5 points NRR impact. Enterprise under 0.5% annual via 60-75% multi-year contracts; mid-market 8% from pricing, but QBRs convert 40% at-risk to flat. Proactive CS with 250 heads, AI health scores predict 90 days out at 92% accuracy, driving 95% renewals. Fixed-fee 85% buffers usage dips like Twilio's; regional strength U.S. 122% NRR. Efficiency Reset saved $45M, sustaining low churn amid budgets—mirroring ServiceNow resilience.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
